client.subtitle: Luxury Goods | Fashion, Fragrance & Beauty
client.description: Chanel is a privately held French luxury fashion house founded by Gabrielle 'Coco' Chanel. The company designs, makes, and sells high-end fashion, fragrances, cosmetics, watches, and fine jewellery through more than 500 directly operated boutiques worldwide. It serves affluent clients globally, with Asia Pacific — including Singapore — as a key and growing market.

priorities.title: Protecting Brand Exclusivity in Digital Channels
priorities.desc: Chanel carefully controls how its brand appears online and offline to protect its image of exclusivity. This means managing digital communications, social content, and client interactions within strict brand guidelines. Teams need to move quickly without compromising the look, tone, or feel of the brand.
priorities.roles: Marketing, Communications, Retail Teams, Client Advisors
priorities.pains: Inconsistent brand voice across regions, slow approval cycles for content, difficulty coordinating messaging between boutiques and head office

priorities.title: Delivering Exceptional Personalised Client Experiences
priorities.desc: Chanel's clients expect a personalised, seamless experience every time they visit a boutique or contact the brand. Building and maintaining strong client relationships requires staff to have the right information at the right moment. AI tools can help advisors prepare better and respond faster.
priorities.roles: Client Advisors, Boutique Managers, CRM Teams, Customer Service
priorities.pains: Fragmented client data across systems, time lost preparing for appointments, difficulty tracking client preferences and purchase history across channels

priorities.title: Scaling Seasonal Collection Launches Globally
priorities.desc: Twice a year, Chanel launches major fashion collections alongside ongoing beauty and fragrance releases. Each launch needs tight coordination across design, production, marketing, retail, and PR teams worldwide. Delays in any one area affect the full launch timeline.
priorities.roles: Product Teams, Marketing, Retail Operations, PR & Communications, Supply Chain
priorities.pains: Long email threads replacing proper briefs, missed deadlines from cross-team misalignment, repetitive status meetings consuming planning time

priorities.title: Advancing Sustainable and Responsible Luxury
priorities.desc: Chanel is committed to reducing its environmental impact while maintaining the quality and craftsmanship it is known for. This involves tracking supplier practices, reporting on sustainability metrics, and embedding responsible sourcing into everyday operations. Reporting and compliance work is growing in volume and complexity.
priorities.roles: Sustainability Teams, Procurement, Finance, Legal & Compliance
priorities.pains: Manual data collection across suppliers, difficulty consolidating sustainability reports, time-consuming ESG disclosure and regulatory filing processes

priorities.title: Building a Future-Ready Global Workforce
priorities.desc: Chanel is investing in attracting, developing, and retaining skilled people across all parts of the business. This includes upskilling staff in digital tools, supporting career growth, and maintaining the craft knowledge that defines the brand. HR and learning teams need better tools to manage this at scale.
priorities.roles: HR, Learning & Development, People Managers, Talent Acquisition
priorities.pains: Learning materials scattered across shared drives, onboarding that takes too long, difficulty tracking skills development and training completion across global teams

capabilities.objectives: Office staff support the business by handling communications, preparing documents, and keeping day-to-day operations running. They work across departments and often bridge information between teams. At Chanel, this group plays a key role in maintaining the high standards of output the brand requires. Their work directly affects how quickly decisions get made and how well teams stay aligned.
capabilities.painPoints: Staff write common documents like briefs and reports from scratch, even for recurring tasks. Emails go back and forth unnecessarily before a clear answer is reached. Finding the right file version across SharePoint and email is time-consuming. Meeting notes are rarely captured well, so follow-ups get missed.
capabilities.keyActivities: drafting internal briefs and memos, formatting presentation decks for leadership, managing inbox and responding to cross-department queries, scheduling and preparing agendas for recurring meetings, updating shared documents on SharePoint, summarising reports for non-specialist readers

capabilities.objectives: Managers at Chanel lead teams across boutiques, regional offices, and head office functions. They are responsible for team performance, project delivery, and upholding brand standards. They translate strategic direction into day-to-day tasks for their teams. Good managers keep projects moving and staff motivated.
capabilities.painPoints: Managers spend too much time in status update meetings instead of focused work. Writing performance reviews and team communications takes longer than it should. Tracking action items across multiple Teams chats and email threads is error-prone. Preparing for one-on-ones and team briefings means pulling information from many different places.
capabilities.keyActivities: running weekly team check-ins and setting action items, writing staff performance notes and review summaries, reviewing project status across boutique or department deliverables, preparing briefs for seasonal launches or campaigns, escalating issues to regional leadership, tracking team training completion

capabilities.objectives: Finance and operations teams manage budgets, forecasts, and the flow of goods and money across Chanel's business. They produce reports that help leaders make decisions on stock, investment, and costs. In a business with multiple product lines and global boutiques, accuracy and speed in financial reporting matter greatly. Operations teams also manage the logistics behind collection launches and product supply.
capabilities.painPoints: Building monthly financial reports in Excel takes significant manual effort and is prone to errors. Consolidating data from multiple boutiques and regions into one view is slow. Finance staff spend time chasing approvals via email rather than through a clear workflow. Explaining financial data to non-finance stakeholders in plain language is a recurring challenge.
capabilities.keyActivities: preparing monthly budget-to-actual reports, consolidating sales and margin data from boutiques, reviewing supplier invoices and purchase orders, building Excel models for seasonal forecasting, drafting financial summaries for regional leadership, tracking operational KPIs across product lines

capabilities.objectives: HR and learning teams at Chanel recruit talent, support employee development, and manage the people processes that keep the business running well. They look after onboarding, benefits, compliance, and learning programmes. As Chanel grows and invests in its workforce, HR handles more work without a proportional increase in team size. Keeping staff engaged and developing their skills is a top priority.
capabilities.painPoints: Onboarding documents exist in different formats and locations, making it hard for new staff to get up to speed. Scheduling interviews across hiring managers wastes time. Writing job descriptions, training content, and policy documents from scratch is time-consuming. Tracking learning completion and skills data across global teams is difficult without better tools.
capabilities.keyActivities: writing job postings and position descriptions, coordinating interview schedules across hiring managers, preparing onboarding packs for new boutique and office staff, drafting HR policy documents and internal communications, tracking training completion and learning records, summarising employee survey results for leadership

capabilities.objectives: Client Advisors and customer service teams are the face of Chanel. They build relationships with clients, guide them through purchases, and deliver a standard of service that matches the brand's prestige. In Singapore and across Asia Pacific, this team handles high-value clients who expect personalised attention. Strong client knowledge and communication skills are essential to this role.
capabilities.painPoints: Preparing for client appointments means pulling information from multiple systems, which takes time before each visit. Writing personalised follow-up notes after interactions is done manually and inconsistently. Responding to client queries by email requires careful brand-tone writing, which is time-intensive. Boutique teams struggle to share client insights across locations in a structured way.
capabilities.keyActivities: preparing client profiles and briefing notes before appointments, writing personalised thank-you and follow-up messages to clients, responding to email and phone enquiries from walk-in and existing clients, logging client interactions and purchase preferences in CRM, handling product availability enquiries across boutiques, escalating client complaints to boutique management

capabilities.objectives: IT teams manage the systems, devices, and platforms that keep Chanel's business running. They support retail point-of-sale systems, corporate applications, and the Microsoft 365 environment. In a luxury business, system downtime has an immediate impact on client experience and sales. IT also leads the rollout of new tools including Microsoft 365 Copilot.
capabilities.painPoints: IT support tickets are handled through email and manual tracking, making it hard to prioritise and resolve issues quickly. Writing clear technical documentation for non-technical users is time-consuming. Coordinating system updates across global time zones is complex. Communicating IT changes to boutique staff in plain, simple language is a recurring challenge.
capabilities.keyActivities: managing Microsoft 365 user accounts and access permissions, supporting boutique POS system issues and escalations, writing technical guides and user-facing how-to documents, coordinating software rollouts across Singapore boutiques, monitoring system availability and flagging incidents, preparing IT reports for regional management

workflows.name: Seasonal Collection Launch

steps.d: Design and marketing teams align on the season's themes, products, and key messages.
Marketing creates campaign materials, look books, and product copy across all channels.
Boutique managers receive launch guides covering stock, merchandising, and client messaging.
Client Advisors are trained on new products and how to present them to clients.
Boutiques open the collection to clients, with outreach sent to VIC client lists.
Sales data and client feedback are collected and shared with leadership for review.

workflows.friction: Briefing documents are sent via email with multiple attachments, causing version confusion. Boutique staff frequently miss updates because information is spread across emails, chats, and shared drives.

workflows.name: Client Appointment Management

steps.d: Client Advisor or boutique receptionist schedules a private client appointment via calendar.
Advisor reviews client purchase history, preferences, and notes from prior visits.
Advisor selects and reserves relevant items based on the client's profile and interests.
Advisor meets the client, presents curated products, and gives personalised styling guidance.
Advisor sends a personalised thank-you note and logs the interaction in CRM.

workflows.friction: Pulling client information from multiple systems before each appointment takes too long. Writing personalised follow-up notes manually after every visit is time-consuming and often skipped.

workflows.name: Monthly Performance Reporting

steps.d: Finance teams pull sales, margin, and inventory data from multiple source systems.
Analysts consolidate data into Excel and build summary tables and charts for leadership.
Finance managers write commentary explaining performance trends and key variances.
Regional leadership reviews the draft report and requests changes before sign-off.
The final report is shared via email or posted to a SharePoint folder.

workflows.friction: Building reports manually in Excel each month is slow and error-prone. Writing clear commentary for non-finance readers takes time and several revision rounds.

workflows.name: Meeting Management and Follow-Up

steps.d: Organiser sends a Teams or Outlook calendar invite with an agenda attached.
Participants review briefing documents or prior meeting notes before joining the call.
Teams meeting is held with discussion, decisions, and action items identified.
Someone manually captures meeting notes and emails a summary to all attendees.
Action owners update progress via email threads or informal Teams messages.

workflows.friction: Meeting notes are often incomplete or arrive late, so follow-ups fall through the gaps. There is no consistent way to track action items, leading to the same topics recurring in the next meeting.

glossary.d: The French word for 'house', used to refer to Chanel as a brand and institution. Employees often say 'the Maison' to mean the company and its heritage.
The craft knowledge and skill embedded in Chanel's products and processes. Preserving savoir-faire is a key part of Chanel's identity and business strategy.
A specialist workshop where skilled artisans produce Chanel garments, accessories, or jewellery by hand. Ateliers are central to Haute Couture and Métiers d'Art production.
Chanel's network of craft workshops acquired to preserve traditional artisan skills. Each Métier specialises in one craft such as embroidery, featherwork, or goldsmithing.
Ready-to-Wear — Chanel's main seasonal fashion line sold in boutiques globally. RTW collections are shown twice a year and are a core driver of retail revenue.
Chanel's highest-end fashion line, made entirely by hand to individual client measurements. Haute Couture is shown in Paris each season and is not available in general retail.
Fragrance & Beauty — Chanel's division covering perfumes, skincare, and makeup. F&B is one of the largest revenue contributors across the business globally.
Watches & Fine Jewellery — the division managing Chanel's luxury timepieces and jewellery. This division operates through dedicated boutiques and selected retail partners.
Very Important Client — Chanel's term for top-tier clients who receive priority service and bespoke experiences. VIC relationship management is a key focus for boutique teams.
The title used for Chanel's in-boutique sales and relationship staff. Client Advisors provide expert product guidance and build long-term client relationships.
A Client Advisor's personal record of client contact details, preferences, and relationship notes. A strong client book signals an experienced and well-connected advisor.
The leader responsible for day-to-day boutique operations, team performance, and client experience. Boutique Managers report to a Zone or Regional Director.
A senior leader overseeing multiple boutiques within a geographic zone. Zone Directors are responsible for sales performance, staff development, and brand standards in their area.
A visual product guide showing how items from a new collection can be worn or styled. Look books are used for staff training and client presentations.
An exclusive in-boutique event where a broader product selection is shown to selected clients, often before general availability. Trunk shows are a key tool for engaging VIC clients.
The arrangement and presentation of products and displays inside a boutique. Chanel's visual merchandising standards are set globally and applied consistently worldwide.
The percentage of inventory sold within a given period, used to measure how well a collection is performing. A high sell-through rate signals strong demand and good product selection.
Smaller fashion collections released between the main seasonal shows, also called Cruise or Resort lines. Pre-collections give boutiques fresh product to sell outside the main fashion calendar.
The difference between revenue and the cost of making goods sold, expressed as a percentage. Chanel's gross margins are high relative to the broader fashion industry.
Environmental, Social, and Governance — the framework Chanel uses to report on sustainability and ethical business practices. ESG reporting is growing in regulatory importance across markets.
The seasonal industry event where Chanel presents its RTW and Haute Couture collections in Paris. Fashion Week is a critical moment for brand visibility and press coverage.
Chanel sells only through its own boutiques and selected channels, not through mass retailers. This controls the client experience and protects the brand's positioning.
A retail model built around exclusive products, premium pricing, and high-touch service. At Chanel, client experience and brand prestige drive purchasing decisions as much as the product does.
An AI assistant built into Microsoft 365 apps like Word, Outlook, and Teams. It helps users write, summarise, and analyse content faster using AI.
Microsoft's document management and intranet platform used for storing and sharing files across teams. At Chanel, SharePoint hosts brand guidelines, policies, and operational documents.
Chanel's main platform for internal messaging, video calls, and file sharing. It connects boutique teams, regional offices, and global headquarters in one place.
Chanel's enterprise resource planning system for managing finance, procurement, and supply chain. It is the primary system of record for financial transactions and inventory data.
The customer relationship management platform storing Chanel's client profiles and purchase records. Boutique teams use it to manage client relationships and log visit interactions.
Chanel's point-of-sale system used in boutiques to process transactions and manage stock. It connects boutique sales data to broader inventory and reporting systems.
A Microsoft 365 tool that surfaces training content inside Teams for easy access. Chanel uses it to deliver product training and compliance courses to staff.
The process of integrating a new employee into Chanel's culture, systems, and role. Effective onboarding includes brand education, product knowledge training, and tool access setup.
The HR function responsible for employee training, skill-building, and career growth. At Chanel, L&D covers product knowledge, leadership skills, and digital tool adoption.
A structured conversation between a manager and employee about goals and progress. At Chanel, reviews are tied to both sales results and how well staff embody brand standards.
The process of introducing AI tools like Microsoft 365 Copilot into everyday work routines. Chanel's AI adoption goal is to help staff work more efficiently while maintaining brand quality.
The executive leading Chanel's operations in a major region such as Asia Pacific or the Americas. Regional Presidents report to global leadership and set market strategy for their region.
